prompt:
A car of mass 1200 kg travels up a straight slope inclined at an angle of 3.5 degrees to the horizontal at a constant speed of 18 m s^-1. A constant resistive force of 420 N opposes the motion. Take g = 9.81 m s^-2.
Calculate:
(a) the component of the car's weight acting down the incline [1]
(b) the forward driving force required to maintain the speed of 18 m s^-1 [1]
(c) the useful mechanical power output delivered by the engine [1]

mark_scheme.criterion: (a) Calculates weight component: mg sin theta = 1200 * 9.81 * sin 3.5 degrees = 719 N (accept 720 N).
(b) Calculates driving force: F = 420 + 718.7 = 1140 N (accept 1139 N).
(c) Calculates power: P = Fv = 1138.7 * 18 = 20 500 W (accept 2.0 * 10^4 W or 20.5 kW).

hints: In (a), resolve weight parallel to slope: W_parallel = mg sin theta.
In (b), add the resistive force to the downhill weight component.
solution:
(a) W_parallel = mg sin 3.5 degrees = 1200 * 9.81 * sin 3.5 degrees = 718.66 N approx 719 N.
(b) F_drive = 420 + 718.66 = 1138.66 N approx 1140 N.
(c) P = Fv = 1138.66 * 18 = 20 496 W approx 20.5 kW.
teacher_walkthrough: Part (a): Component along incline = mg sin theta = 1200 * 9.81 * 0.06105 = 718.7 N.
Part (b): Resultant force is zero, so forward force = resistance + weight component = 420 + 718.7 = 1138.7 N.
